editorial.headline: Motorcycle Passenger Transport, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers motorcycle-based passenger transport, including online ojek services and motorcycle hire with a driver or operator.
editorial.body:
Motorcycle passenger transport is a defined operating business, not simply the use of a motorcycle to get someone from one place to another. Its scope includes carrying passengers on two-wheeled motor vehicles through conventional motorcycle-taxi services and app-based ojek services. It also includes hiring out a motorcycle together with a driver or operator. The common thread is clear: the business is organised around passenger movement by motorcycle, whether the service is ordered directly, coordinated digitally, or supplied as a vehicle-and-driver arrangement.

The record opens this activity to medium and large enterprises. That framing matters because it places the code in a business context beyond an informal description of motorcycle work: the registered activity encompasses an enterprise providing and organising passenger transport by two-wheeled vehicle. The scope is broad enough to include both conventional and online modes, yet specific about the vehicle and service model. A business relying on this classification should therefore be able to describe its real operation in those terms: transporting passengers by motorcycle, or providing a motorcycle with its driver or operator.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In practical terms, the record does not impose a national foreign-equity cap below full ownership for this activity. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. That is the national picture: an activity open to foreign investment at up to 100%, for the medium and large scales identified in the record.

Bali requires a separate reading, and it is more precise than a blanket assumption about foreign-owned businesses on the island. This activity is not blocked by Bali’s moratorium because it is recorded as medium-high or high risk, rather than within the low and medium-low risk categories covered by that province-wide, permanent restriction on PMA registration. Its Bali status is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The remaining instruction is practical rather than prohibitive: verify the position for the specific address. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali closes this activity to foreign investment today; it is that the moratorium does not block it, while the address still needs to be checked.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally open to 100% foreign ownership, this activity is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium, though the specific address still requires verification.
